newsitem.title: INDIA: De Beers pulls out of Indian diamond mine.
newsitem.headline: De Beers pulls out of Indian diamond mine.

text.p: South African mining giant De Beers has decided against bidding for diamond mining rights in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh, a senior state government official said on Saturday.
De Beers was the top bidder for the mines, followed by Australia's Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd, formerly RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd, and Ashton Mining Ltd.

The official in the state's mining department said De Beers last week decided against bidding for the tenders after the government refused to let it sell diamonds mined in Madhya Pradesh through the firm's Central Selling Organisation (CSO).

The official, who asked not to be named, said state chief minister Digvijay Singh told De Beers executive director Robin Crawford that the government planned to sell the diamonds through an open auction.
India is the world's largest exporter of cut and polished diamonds. It imports most of its roughs, the bulk of which come from the powerful CSO.

The Madhya Pradesh government in January backtracked on a decision to award De Beers a lease to mine diamonds in the state and said it would float fresh tenders for diamond prospecting later in the year.
De Beers has already set up a 50-50 joint venture with India's Reliance Industries Ltd to mine diamonds in Madhya Pradesh.
